symbols.name: \mathfrak E
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak E=(\mathcal X,\mathcal A,\phi,\pi_{\mathrm{ref}},\eta)\) is fixed and publicly supplied to every learner.

symbols.name: P^{\otimes n}
symbols.def: the product observation law induced by the one-observation law \(P\)

symbols.name: J_{\eta,P}
symbols.def:
The paper uses the standard extended reverse-KL convention \(p\log(p/0)=+\infty\) for \(p>0\) and \(0\log(0/q)=0\). Thus
\[
J_{\eta,P}(\pi)=\mathbb E_{X\sim\rho,A\sim\pi(\cdot\mid X)}r_\theta(X,A)-\eta^{-1}\mathbb E_{X\sim\rho}\operatorname{KL}(\pi(\cdot\mid X)\Vert\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid X)).
\]
If \(\rho(x)>0\) and \(\pi(a\mid x)>0=\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(a\mid x)\) for some action, then \(J_{\eta,P}(\pi)=-\infty\). On policies satisfying \(\operatorname{supp}\pi(\cdot\mid x)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid x)\) for every context, this functional is finite and its restriction is real valued.
symbols.role: extended regularized welfare with a finite reference-supported restriction

symbols.name: \pi_P^\star
symbols.def: \(\pi_P^\star(a\mid x)=\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(a\mid x)\exp\{\eta r_\theta(x,a)\}/\sum_{b\in\mathcal A}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(b\mid x)\exp\{\eta r_\theta(x,b)\}\)

symbols.name: \underline J_n
symbols.sig: \(\underline J_n:\{\pi\in\Delta(\mathcal A)^{\mathcal X}:\operatorname{supp}\pi(\cdot\mid x)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X\}\to\mathbb R\)
symbols.def: Diagnostic empirical pessimistic welfare criterion evaluated only on reference-supported policies; it does not define \(\widehat\pi\). Every Gibbs learner constructed in the note is automatically reference supported.

symbols.name: \widehat\pi
symbols.def: \(\widehat\pi\) is the Gibbs policy generated by the coordinatewise lower envelope of \(\mathcal Q_n\), as specified in \(\text{def:prediction-polytope-learner}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal L_n(\mathfrak E)
symbols.space: measurable maps from \((S\times[0,1])^n\times\{\mathfrak E\}\) to \(\{\pi\in\Delta(\mathcal A)^{\mathcal X}:\operatorname{supp}\pi(\cdot\mid x)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X\}\)
symbols.def: The effective minimax decision class consists of sample-measurable policy learners whose every output is supported on the public reference policy. The support condition depends only on \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\), hence the class is law-independent. Under the extended reverse-KL convention, its minimax infimum equals the infimum over all measurable full-simplex policy learners, because the public measurable support repair in \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\) never increases regret.
symbols.role: finite-objective minimax decision class, without loss relative to the full-simplex class

symbols.name: e_0,u_j,w_j,z
symbols.def: orthonormal basis vectors, with \(z\) used only when \(d\) is even

symbols.name: e_{(x,a)}
symbols.def: canonical coordinate vector indexed by \((x,a)\in S\)

symbols.name: x_C,x_A,x_j,x_z
symbols.def: pointwise-calibration, anchor, hard, and optional unused-coordinate contexts

symbols.name: v
symbols.def: index of a paired-Bernoulli hard instance

symbols.name: \mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)
symbols.space: sets of specifications \(P\) compatible with \(\mathfrak E\)

symbols.name: \mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)
symbols.def: abbreviation for \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)\) after \(\mathfrak E\) is fixed and no experiments are compared

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_{n,\mathfrak E}
symbols.sig: \(\mathfrak R_{n,\mathfrak E}:\{\mathcal M\ne\varnothing:\mathcal M\text{ consists of laws compatible with }\mathfrak E\}\to\mathbb R_+\)
symbols.def: Minimax expected regularized suboptimality conditional on \(\mathfrak E\), computed over measurable reference-supported learners. Its value is exactly the same as the full-simplex extended-reverse-KL minimax value. It is a nonnegative real number because the public reference learner is supported and has finite regret.
symbols.role: risk frontier under an equivalent finite-objective decision representation

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_n
symbols.def: Abbreviation for the nonnegative real functional \(\mathfrak R_{n,\mathfrak E}\) after \(\mathfrak E\) is fixed and no experiments are compared; it inherits the exact equivalence between the supported finite-objective and full-simplex extended-reverse-KL formulations.
symbols.role: fixed-experiment risk abbreviation under the equivalent finite-objective representation

symbols.name: N^\star_{\mathfrak E}
symbols.def: exact-shell minimax sample complexity conditional on the explicit public experiment \(\mathfrak E\)

symbols.name: N^\star
symbols.def: abbreviation for \(N^\star_{\mathfrak E}\) after \(\mathfrak E\) is fixed and no experiments are compared

symbols.name: \widehat\pi_{\mathrm{ERM}}
symbols.def: The Gibbs policy generated by the sequentially selected empirical-risk minimizer \(\widehat f\), as specified in \(\text{def:erm-gibbs-plugin-learner}\).

novel.justification: The maximum target-to-logging likelihood ratio is an auditable finite-support property that defines a deployment coverage tier independently of an estimation procedure.
The target-versus-logging generalized eigenvalue is a representation-aware coverage diagnostic determined by the law and feature map.

definitions.name: common public-design experiment
definitions.construction: Fix the finite supports \(\mathcal X,\mathcal A\), carrying their intended discrete/Borel measurable structures, the known feature map \(\phi\), the known reference and logging policy \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\), and \(\eta\) as \(\mathfrak E=(\mathcal X,\mathcal A,\phi,\pi_{\mathrm{ref}},\eta)\). The context distribution \(\rho\) is not a component of \(\mathfrak E\); it remains law-specific. For every compatible one-observation law \(P\), \(\mathcal D_n\sim P^{\otimes n}\). A learner is an element of \(\mathcal L_n(\mathfrak E)\), so it receives \(\mathcal D_n\) and \(\mathfrak E\), returns a policy, and is supported on \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\) at every context. Because \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\) is public, this support requirement is law-independent and uses only public design inputs. By \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\), it is without loss relative to the class of all measurable full-simplex policy learners under the extended reverse-KL convention. Write \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)\), \(\mathfrak R_{n,\mathfrak E}\), and \(N^\star_{\mathfrak E}\) whenever public experiments are compared. The unindexed notation \(\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)\), \(\mathfrak R_n\), and \(N^\star\) is an abbreviation only after one \(\mathfrak E\) has been fixed and no cross-experiment comparison is being made.

definitions.name: exact linear reverse-KL shell conditional on a public experiment
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)=\{P:\ P\text{ is compatible with the fixed public experiment }\mathfrak E,\ \rho\text{ is the context distribution supplied by }P,\text{ and ass:finite-contexts, ass:finite-actions, ass:bounded-features, ass:linear-realizability, ass:reference-logging, ass:nonsingular-logging-geometry, ass:pointwise-exact-shell, and ass:feature-exact-shell hold for }P\}\). When \(\mathfrak E\) is fixed and no experiments are compared, write \(\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)=\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)\).

definitions.name: invariant prediction-polytope pessimistic learner
definitions.construction:
Let \(S=\mathcal X\times\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal F=\{f\in[0,1]^S:\exists\theta\in\mathbb R^d,\ f(x,a)=\phi(x,a)^\top\theta\}\). Fix once and for all a lexicographic order of \(S\). Set \(L_n(f)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(Y_i-f(X_i,A_i))^2\), and let \(\widehat f\) be the sequentially lexicographically selected minimizer of \(L_n\) over the compact polytope \(\mathcal F\). Define \(\|h\|_n^2=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nh(X_i,A_i)^2\) and \(\mathcal Q_n=\{f\in\mathcal F:\|f-\widehat f\|_n^2\le c_0[d\log(en)+\log(2n^2)]/n\}\). The set \(\mathcal Q_n\) is nonempty and compact because it contains \(\widehat f\). For every \((x,a)\in S\), define the unique minimum value \(\underline r_n(x,a)=\min_{f\in\mathcal Q_n}f(x,a)\); if an attaining witness is needed, select one sequentially lexicographically using the fixed order of \(S\). Define the deployed policy at every context, observed or unobserved, by
\[
\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(a\mid x)e^{\eta\underline r_n(x,a)}}{\sum_{b\in\mathcal A}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(b\mid x)e^{\eta\underline r_n(x,b)}}.
\]
This Gibbs policy satisfies \(\operatorname{supp}\widehat\pi(\cdot\mid x)=\operatorname{supp}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid x)\) for every context and therefore belongs to the finite-objective decision class. For reference-supported policies \(\pi\), retain \(\underline J_n(\pi)=\inf_{f\in\mathcal Q_n}[n^{-1}\sum_i\sum_a\pi(a\mid X_i)f(X_i,a)-(\eta n)^{-1}\sum_i\operatorname{KL}(\pi(\cdot\mid X_i)\Vert\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid X_i))]\) as the empirical pessimistic criterion; no real-valued off-support evaluation is intended. In any feature coordinates, \(\|f_\theta-f_{\widehat\theta}\|_n^2=(\theta-\widehat\theta)^\top\widehat\Sigma_n(\theta-\widehat\theta)\), where \(\widehat\Sigma_n=n^{-1}\sum_i\phi(X_i,A_i)\phi(X_i,A_i)^\top\); this equality is notation only and no coefficient representative is selected.

definitions.name: public-experiment-indexed exact-shell minimax risk
definitions.construction:
For a fixed public experiment \(\mathfrak E\) and every nonempty class \(\mathcal M\) of laws compatible with \(\mathfrak E\), use the standard extended reverse-KL convention in \(J_{\eta,P}\). Thus a policy that assigns positive mass outside \(\operatorname{supp}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid x)\) at any context with positive \(\rho\)-mass has objective \(-\infty\) and regret \(+\infty\). For an arbitrary policy \(\pi\), define the public contextwise support repair
\[
(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{ref}}\pi)(a\mid x)=
\begin{cases}
\pi(a\mid x),&\pi(b\mid x)=0\text{ for every }b\text{ such that }\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(b\mid x)=0,\\
\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(a\mid x),&\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]
Because the supports have the standing finite discrete/Borel measurable structures, \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{ref}}\) is Borel measurable and sends every measurable policy learner to an element of \(\mathcal L_n(\mathfrak E)\). For every law and every realized learner output, its repair leaves the objective unchanged when every offending context has zero \(\rho\)-mass, while otherwise the unrepaired regret is \(+\infty\) and the repaired regret is finite. Hence repair never increases regret. Since supported learners are themselves full-simplex learners, the two infima are equal, and their common value is
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,\mathfrak E}(\mathcal M)=\inf_{\widetilde\pi\in\mathcal L_n(\mathfrak E)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\left[J_{\eta,P}(\pi_P^\star)-J_{\eta,P}(\widetilde\pi(\mathcal D_n;\mathfrak E))\right].
\]
Equivalently, the right-hand side equals the same infimum taken over all measurable full-simplex policy-valued learners with the displayed loss interpreted in \([0,+\infty]\). The Gibbs optimum has exactly the support of \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\), and the public reference learner has finite regret, so the common minimax value is a nonnegative real number. When \(\mathfrak E\) is fixed and no experiments are compared, write \(\mathfrak R_n=\mathfrak R_{n,\mathfrak E}\).

definitions.name: public-experiment-indexed exact-shell sample complexity
definitions.construction:
For \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)\ne\varnothing\), define
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)=\inf\left\{n\in\mathbb N:\mathfrak R_{n,\mathfrak E}\bigl(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)\bigr)\le\epsilon\right\},
\]
with the convention \(\inf\varnothing=\infty\). When \(\mathfrak E\) is fixed and no experiments are compared, write \(N^\star=N^\star_{\mathfrak E}\).

definitions.name: feasible-frontier handle
definitions.construction: Handle: derive the joint Gibbs feasibility constraints for \(C_P\) and \(D_P\), then construct covariance-preserving lower families or prove their nonexistence.

definitions.name: explicit paired-Bernoulli exact-shell family
definitions.construction:
For \((C,D)\in\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{hard}}^\circ(d,\eta)\), put \(k=\lfloor(d-1)/2\rfloor\), take an orthonormal basis \(e_0,(u_j,w_j)_{j=1}^k\), and add \(z\) when \(d\) is even. Use actions \(\{+,-,0\}\). At \(x_C\), set \(q=(e^\eta/C-1)/(e^\eta-1)\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(+\mid x_C)=q\), distribute \(1-q\) positively over \(-,0\), and set \(\phi(x_C,+)=e_0\), \(\phi(x_C,-)=\phi(x_C,0)=0\), and \(\theta_0=1\). Put \(A=q(C-D)/(D-1)\), add \(x_A\) when \(C>D\) with every action feature equal to \(e_0\), give \(x_C\) raw mass \(\tau=[4(1+A)]^{-1}\) and \(x_A\) raw mass \(\tau A\), and give the hard contexts total raw mass one. When \(z\) is present, add \(x_z\) with raw mass \(1/4\), every action feature \(z\), and coefficient zero. Normalize these raw masses to define \(\rho\). At each \(x_j\), of raw mass \(1/k\), put \(p=(4D)^{-1}\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(+\mid x_j)=\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(-\mid x_j)=p\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(0\mid x_j)=1-2p\), \(\phi(x_j,+)=(u_j+w_j)/\sqrt2\), \(\phi(x_j,-)=(u_j-w_j)/\sqrt2\), and \(\phi(x_j,0)=0\). For \(v\in\{-1,1\}^k\), let \(T_\gamma=D(1-2p)/[e^{\eta\gamma}-2pD\cosh(\eta\gamma)]\), \(\beta=\eta^{-1}\log T_\gamma\), and \(\theta_{u_j}=\sqrt2\beta\), \(\theta_{w_j}=\sqrt2\gamma v_j\), so \(r_v(x_j,\pm)=\beta\pm\gamma v_j\). Define
\[
g_0(D,\eta)=\sup\left\{g>0:\text{ for every }s\in[0,g],\ e^{\eta s}-2pD\cosh(\eta s)>0\text{ and }s\le\eta^{-1}\log T_s\le1-s\right\},
\]
and set \(\gamma(\epsilon,d,C,D,\eta)=\eta^{-1}\operatorname{arcosh}(e^{64\eta\epsilon})\). The family \(\mathcal H_{d,C,D,\eta,\epsilon}\) comprises these \(2^k\) Bernoulli laws whenever \(\gamma\le\min\{g_0(D,\eta),1/4,\beta,1-\beta\}\).

definitions.name: empirical-risk-minimizer Gibbs plug-in learner
definitions.construction:
Using the sequentially lexicographically selected empirical-risk minimizer \(\widehat f\in\mathcal F\) from \(\text{def:prediction-polytope-learner}\), define, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\),
\[
\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{ERM}}(a\mid x)
=\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(a\mid x)e^{\eta\widehat f(x,a)}}{\sum_{b\in\mathcal A}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(b\mid x)e^{\eta\widehat f(x,b)}}.
\]
The learner receives only \((\mathcal D_n,\mathfrak E)\); it does not receive the shell indices \(C\) or \(D\).

statements.statement: If the shell \(\mathcal M(d,1,1,\eta)\) is nonempty, then every \(P\) in it has \(\pi_P^\star=\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\) \(\rho\)-almost surely, \(D_P=1\), and \(J_{\eta,P}(\pi_P^\star)-J_{\eta,P}(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})=0\). Hence \(N^\star(\epsilon;d,1,1,\eta)=1\) for every \(\epsilon>0\).
statements.justification: A conditional likelihood ratio has reference mean one, so an essential supremum of one forces equality of the target and reference policies.
statements.gap: Existing reverse-KL coverage bounds do not separately record the exact-shell \(C=1\) zero-risk boundary.
statements.consumer: It prevents a coverage diagnostic from assigning a positive sample requirement when the known reference policy is already optimal.

statements.statement: Under every invertible reparameterization \(\phi\mapsto T\phi\) and \(\theta\mapsto T^{-\top}\theta\), the prediction polytope \(\mathcal F\), the selected function \(\widehat f\), the confidence set \(\mathcal Q_n\), the criterion \(\underline J_n\), and the selected policy \(\widehat\pi\) are unchanged.
statements.justification: The learner is defined entirely in prediction space, so invertible feature-coordinate changes leave every deployed probability and the diagnostic criterion unchanged.
statements.gap: This is coordinate-free implementation infrastructure rather than the statistical novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It permits whitening and other invertible feature changes without altering the learner at observed or unobserved contexts.

statements.statement:
There are universal constants such that, after choosing \(c_0\) sufficiently large and whenever \(\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)\ne\varnothing\), the lower-envelope Gibbs learner \(\widehat\pi\in\mathcal L_n(\mathfrak E)\) uses neither \(C\) nor \(D\) as input and satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}[J_{\eta,P}(\pi_P^\star)-J_{\eta,P}(\widehat\pi)]
\le\widetilde O\left(\min\left\{\frac{\eta d^2D}{n},\sqrt{\frac{d^2D}{n}}\right\}\right)+\delta_n.
\]
The proof derives a distribution-free \(d/n\) logging prediction radius for every member of \(\mathcal Q_n\), a pointwise leverage majorant for the nonlinear lower envelope, the trace inequality \(D_{2,P}\le dD_P\), the Gibbs regret identity, and the endpoint-monotonicity fast and slow conversions. Consequently
\[
N^\star(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)
\le\widetilde O\left(d^2D\min\{\eta/\epsilon,\epsilon^{-2}\}\right)
\]
when the right-hand side is at least two. The additional factor \(d\) is unavoidable for the empirical-ball lower-envelope learner in general: \(\text{prop:empirical-ball-dimension-witness}\) gives exact shells on which the original \(dD\) upper rate fails.
statements.justification: The lower-envelope Gibbs learner remains a valid invariant theorem-local construction with clean temperature dependence.
statements.gap: Its extra factor \(d\) is learner-specific and is superseded for general achievability by \(\text{thm:clean-temperature-feature-upper}\).
statements.consumer: It diagnoses why coordinatewise pessimistic envelopes can lose a dimension factor.

statements.statement: For every \((C,D)\in\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{hard}}^\circ(d,\eta)\), the construction in \(\text{def:explicit-hard-family}\) gives a nonempty shell \(\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)\), has \(g_0(D,\eta)>0\), and has a positive admissible accuracy interval on which \(\mathcal H_{d,C,D,\eta,\epsilon}\subset\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)\). Its members satisfy exactly \(C_P=C\), \(D_P=D\), and \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}\succ0\). There are constants \(\epsilon_1(C,D,\eta)\in(0,\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)]\) and \(c(C,D,\eta)>0\) such that, for every \(0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_1(C,D,\eta)\), \(N^\star(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)\ge c(C,D,\eta)dD\eta/\epsilon\). Thus the displayed paired-Bernoulli family proves the local fast branch; it does not prove the \(\epsilon^{-2}\) branch.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(t=\eta\gamma\) and let \(H\) be the sum of the raw context masses in the construction. Since \(\tau(1+A)=1/4\), \(H=5/4\) for odd \(d\) and \(H=3/2\) for even \(d\). In particular, every hard context has probability \(\rho(x_j)=1/(Hk)\).

First consider admissibility. At \(\gamma=0\),
\[
T_0=\frac{D(1-2p)}{1-2pD}=2D-1.
\]
The hard-region inequalities give \(1<T_0<e^\eta\). Therefore \(\beta_0=\eta^{-1}\log(2D-1)\) lies strictly between zero and one. The denominator defining \(T_\gamma\), the map \(T_\gamma\), and \(\beta_\gamma=\eta^{-1}\log T_\gamma\) are continuous near zero. Hence there is \(\gamma_1>0\), depending only on \(D,\eta\), such that, whenever \(0\le\gamma\le\gamma_1\), the denominator is positive, \(0<\gamma\le\beta_\gamma\le1-\gamma\), and \(t\le1\). This also proves \(g_0(D,\eta)>0\), and consequently \(\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)>0\). By continuity and strict monotonicity of \(\epsilon\mapsto\eta^{-1}\operatorname{arcosh}(e^{64\eta\epsilon})\), choose \(\epsilon_1\in(0,\epsilon_0]\) so that \(\gamma(\epsilon,d,C,D,\eta)\le\min\{\gamma_1,1/4\}\) for \(0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_1\).

We next verify the shell equalities. At \(x_C\), the Gibbs normalizer is
\[
q e^\eta+1-q=e^\eta/C,
\]
so the likelihood ratio of action \(+\) is exactly \(C\), while the ratios of the other actions equal \(C/e^\eta<1\). At each hard context,
\[
Z=1-2p+2pT_\gamma\cosh t.
\]
The defining equation for \(T_\gamma\) is equivalent to
\[
T_\gamma e^t=DZ.
\]
Thus the favored and unfavored informative actions have likelihood ratios \(D\) and \(De^{-2t}\), respectively. Moreover \(T_\gamma e^t\ge1\) because \(\beta_\gamma\ge\gamma\), so the zero-action ratio \(1/Z\) is at most \(D\). At \(x_A\), and at \(x_z\) when present, every action has the same reward and the likelihood ratio is one. Since \(D\le C\), the global essential supremum is exactly \(C\).

All covariance blocks are diagonal except for the two-dimensional hard blocks. In the \(e_0\) direction, the target-to-logging variance ratio is
\[
\frac{qC+A}{q+A}=D,
\qquad
A=\frac{q(C-D)}{D-1}.
\]
In the basis \((u_j,w_j)\), the logging block is a positive multiple of \(pI_2\). After whitening, the target block has eigenvalues \(D\) and \(De^{-2t}\). The optional \(z\) block has ratio one. Every basis direction receives positive logging mass, so \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}\succ0\), and the largest generalized eigenvalue is exactly \(D\). The reward means are in \([0,1]\) by the choice of \(\gamma_1\), and the features have norm at most one. Taking the conditional reward to be Bernoulli with the displayed mean verifies every remaining condition of the exact shell. Thus \(\mathcal H_{d,C,D,\eta,\epsilon}\subset\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)\).

It remains to prove the local lower bound. At a hard context, the two Gibbs action laws corresponding to the two signs are
\[
s_+=(a,b,c),\qquad s_-=(b,a,c),\qquad a=pD=\frac14,\quad b=ae^{-2t},\quad c=1-a-b.
\]
For any action distribution \(u\), the Gibbs variational identity gives the sum of the two regularized regrets as
\[
\eta^{-1}\{\operatorname{KL}(u\Vert s_+)+\operatorname{KL}(u\Vert s_-)\}.
\]
Minimizing over \(u\) yields minus twice the logarithm of the Bhattacharyya affinity, and hence
\[
\inf_u\eta^{-1}\{\operatorname{KL}(u\Vert s_+)+\operatorname{KL}(u\Vert s_-)\}
=-\frac2\eta\log\{1-a(1-e^{-t})^2\}
\ge \frac{t^2}{8\eta},
\]
where the last inequality uses \(t\le1\), \(1-e^{-t}\ge t/2\), and \(-\log(1-z)\ge z\).

Neighboring sign vectors differ only at one hard context. Shrinking \(\gamma_1\) if necessary, continuity of \(\beta_\gamma\) ensures that all four Bernoulli means \(\beta_\gamma\pm\gamma\) lie in a fixed compact subinterval of \((0,1)\). The elementary Bernoulli inequality
\[
\operatorname{kl}(u\Vert v)\le\frac{(u-v)^2}{v(1-v)}
\]
therefore shows that the Kullback--Leibler divergence between the \(n\)-sample laws of two neighbors is at most
\[
K(D,\eta)\,n\rho(x_j)p\gamma^2
=K(D,\eta)\frac{np\gamma^2}{Hk}.
\]
If \(n\le c_1(D,\eta)k/(p\gamma^2)\), Pinsker's inequality, which follows from the scalar inequality \((1+z)\log(1+z)+(1-z)\log(1-z)\ge z^2\), makes the total variation distance between every pair of neighbors at most \(1/2\).

For nonnegative losses \(L_+,L_-\) satisfying \(L_+(u)+L_-(u)\ge s\) pointwise, integration against the minimum of the two neighboring data densities gives
\[
\mathbb E_+L_++\mathbb E_-L_-\ge s\{1-\operatorname{TV}(P_+^{\otimes n},P_-^{\otimes n})\}.
\]
Pair the vertices of the sign cube along each coordinate and average this inequality. Since \(\sum_j\rho(x_j)=1/H\), the Bayes risk under the uniform prior on the cube is at least a fixed positive multiple of \(t^2/\eta\). For \(0\le t\le1\),
\[
\frac{t^2}{3}\le\log\cosh t\le\frac{t^2}{2}.
\]
The calibration \(\log\cosh t=64\eta\epsilon\) therefore makes this Bayes risk strictly larger than \(\epsilon\), after decreasing \(c_1\) if needed. The same inequalities give \(\gamma^2=t^2/\eta^2\le192\epsilon/\eta\). Since \(p=(4D)^{-1}\) and \(k\ge d/4\), the testing condition includes
\[
n\le c_2(C,D,\eta)\frac{dD\eta}{\epsilon}.
\]
The minimax risk over the shell is no smaller than the Bayes risk over its finite subfamily. Hence it exceeds \(\epsilon\) throughout the last range of sample sizes, which proves
\[
N^\star(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)\ge c_2(C,D,\eta)dD\eta/\epsilon
\]
for every \(0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_1\).
statements.justification: The paired-Bernoulli family preserves both exact shell equalities and yields the local fast lower branch on its proved interior hard region.
statements.gap: The construction proves only a pointwise small-accuracy \(\Omega_{C,D,\eta}(d/\epsilon)\) rate; it does not prove a uniform \(D\)- or \(\eta\)-dependence and does not produce a quadratic branch.
statements.consumer: It supplies the informative lower headline that complements, but does not uniformly match, the all-temperature stabilization upper bound.

statements.statement: Under the canonical tabular specialization \(d=|S|\) and \(\phi(x,a)=e_{(x,a)}\), \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1/2}\Lambda_P^\star\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1/2}\) is diagonal with entries \(\pi_P^\star(a\mid x)/\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(a\mid x)\). Hence \(D_P=C_P\), and the exact shell \(\mathcal M(d,C,C,\eta)\) reduces to the canonical tabular reverse-KL shell.
statements.justification: Canonical features diagonalize both the logging and target covariances.
statements.gap: Ji et al., arXiv:2605.02141, study the tabular KL-regularized setting; this proposition gives the required reduction of the shared-linear notation to that setting.
statements.consumer: It makes the tabular fast--slow frontier an auditable special case of the proposed exact-shell vocabulary.

statements.statement: For \(d=5\), every \((C,D)\in\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{hard}}^\circ(5,\eta)\), and every admissible \(\epsilon\), each law in \(\mathcal H_{5,C,D,\eta,\epsilon}\) is a non-tabular shared-feature member: at every hard context \(x_j\), the two action features \(\phi(x_j,+)=(u_j+w_j)/\sqrt2\) and \(\phi(x_j,-)=(u_j-w_j)/\sqrt2\) share both latent directions and are not canonical coordinate indicators.
statements.justification: The lower construction preserves its shell equalities while coupling the two informative action rewards through common feature directions.
statements.gap: The tabular construction in Ji et al. has independent arm coordinates; this exhibits the feature sharing absent from that reduction.
statements.consumer: It makes the claimed linear extension testable on a concrete finite instance rather than on a verbal distinction from tabular bandits.

statements.statement: For the fixed public experiment \(\mathfrak E\), characterize which pairs in the varying-design feasible region of \(\text{thm:feasible-index-region}\) give nonempty exact shells, and determine their minimax frontier outside \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{hard}}^\circ(d,\eta)\). In particular, determine the rates at feasible fixed-design pairs with \(2D-1\ge e^\eta\), prove or refute a matching \(\epsilon^{-2}\) lower branch, and determine whether a learner other than the empirical-ball coordinatewise-envelope learner attains \(\widetilde O(dD\min\{\eta/\epsilon,\epsilon^{-2}\})\). The point \((1,1)\) is already closed by \(\text{thm:zero-risk-boundary}\).
statements.justification: The varying-design feasible region and its zero-risk boundary are proved. The remaining question concerns which nontrivial pairs a specified public experiment supports and the minimax frontier on those fixed-design shells.
statements.gap: The rates for feasible fixed-design pairs with \(2D-1\ge e^\eta\), a matching \(\epsilon^{-2}\) lower branch, and a sharper learner with \(dD\) dimension dependence remain unresolved.
statements.consumer: A resolution would determine whether pointwise coverage \(C\) is genuinely minimax-irrelevant beyond feature coverage \(D\), rather than merely absent from the current upper bound.

sampling_model.design: The finite supports carry their intended discrete/Borel measurable structures. Together with the feature map, reference and logging policy, and inverse temperature, they form the fixed public experiment \(\mathfrak E\). The context distribution \(\rho\) is law-specific, and \(\mathcal D_n\) consists of \(n\) independent observations from \(P\). Learners observe only \((\mathcal D_n,\mathfrak E)\); the stabilized learner does not receive \(\rho\), \(C\), or \(D\). The paper interprets reverse KL in the extended sense. Its effective decision class contains measurable policies supported on the public \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\), which is exactly without loss relative to all measurable full-simplex policy learners because the public contextwise support repair is measurable and never increases regret.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Bounded linear reward prediction is learned by empirical squared-loss minimization over \(\mathcal F\), producing the confidence polytope \(\mathcal Q_n\). The headline stabilization learner chooses the member \(g\in\mathcal Q_n\) minimizing the worst empirical Gibbs-weighted squared radius over \(f\in\mathcal Q_n\), with a fixed measurable lexicographic selector, and deploys the Gibbs policy generated by that \(g\). It uses only the logged sample and the public experiment.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For offline i.i.d. reverse-KL contextual bandits with the reference equal to the behavior policy and a general realizable class \(\mathcal G\), Theorem 2.10 gives, at sufficiently small \(\epsilon\), the high-probability sample-complexity upper bound \(\widetilde O\!\left(\eta D_{\pi^\star}^2\epsilon^{-1}\log N_{\mathcal G}(\epsilon)\right)\). For \(\mathcal G_\Theta=\{\phi^\top\vartheta:\vartheta\in\Theta\}\), its pointwise coefficient is \(D_{\mathcal G}^2((x,a);\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})=\sup_{\delta\in\Theta-\Theta}(\phi(x,a)^\top\delta)^2/(\delta^\top\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}\delta)\). If \(\Theta-\Theta\) contains a nonzero multiple of every needed direction, then this equals \(\phi(x,a)^\top\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1}\phi(x,a)\), so \(D_{\pi^\star}^2=\operatorname{tr}(M)\) for \(M=\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1/2}\Lambda_P^\star\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1/2}\) and \(D_P\le D_{\pi^\star}^2\le dD_P\). The bounded prediction polytope alone does not imply that directional richness; without it one has only \(D_{\mathcal G}^2((x,a);\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})\le\phi(x,a)^\top\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1}\phi(x,a)\), not the trace identity or \(D_P\le D_{\pi^\star}^2\). Theorem 2.11 is an existential lower bound over a class with density-ratio upper bound \(C^\star\), not a lower bound on an exact \((C_P,D_P)\) shell.
It matches fast and slow reverse-KL rates for tabular multi-armed bandits and identifies linear or general function approximation as future work.
Unregularized deterministic-policy pessimism based on coefficient \(\ell_p\) confidence sets; Theorem 1 has \(n^{-1/2}\) regret controlled by a whitened first-moment feature norm.

Policy-transfer coefficients and pseudo-dimension characterize broad unregularized offline classes; Theorems 4.1 and 5.1 give class lower and upper bounds, and Example 3.3 shows zero risk with vacuous concentrability.
Theorems 1, 10, and 15 provide general interactive lower-bound and learnability machinery through interactive Fano, fractional covering, and DEC.
Passive contextual-linear BPI Theorem 2 gives fixed-confidence PAC learnability and a design-matrix information lower bound for unregularized best-policy identification.

tldr: For every fixed finite public experiment with a nonempty exact shell and every \(0<\epsilon<1\), an explicit measurable idealized global-optimization learner achieves the all-temperature sample-complexity bound \(\widetilde O\!\left(dD\min\{\eta/\epsilon,\epsilon^{-2}\}\right)\) without using \(C\), \(D\), or the law-specific context distribution as inputs. The numerical indices do not determine the fixed-design minimax frontier: one experiment can have zero risk for every \(\epsilon>0\), while another has a pointwise local \(\Omega_{C,D,\eta}(d/\epsilon)\) lower bound. There is no uniform lower dependence on \(D\) or \(\eta\), and no positive quadratic lower branch persists through all sufficiently small accuracies.

project_justification.gap: Zhao et al. already give a single-policy fast upper bound for general realizable reverse-KL policy learning and an existential density-ratio lower bound. In a directionally rich linear parameter class their single-policy quantity becomes the trace of the target-versus-logging covariance ratio, whereas the present \(D_P\) is its largest eigenvalue; the bounded prediction polytope alone does not guarantee that trace identity. What is not supplied by the cited literature is the bounded shared-linear exact-shell combination developed here: an all-temperature expected-minimax upper bound of order \(dD_P\) up to logarithms, uniform over a fixed exact shell; a finite fixed-experiment feasibility certificate for simultaneous exact \((C_P,D_P)\); and a same-index comparison between a zero-risk public experiment and an experiment with pointwise-local \(d/\epsilon\) difficulty.
project_justification.niche: The note studies reverse-KL-regularized offline linear contextual-bandit policy learning on exact shells indexed jointly by pointwise coverage \(C\) and generalized-eigenvalue feature coverage \(D\), conditional on a fixed public experiment.
project_justification.fill: It gives a finite exponential nonlinear-semidefinite certificate for fixed-design shell nonemptiness, an explicit measurable idealized global-optimization learner with the universal clean \(dD\) upper order at every temperature, and experiment-specific witnesses proving that the exact \((d,C,D,\eta)\) indices do not determine the fixed-design frontier. The contribution is specialized to reverse-KL exact shells: it does not claim the general principle that coverage summaries can be insufficient, and its only informative lower comparison is pointwise and local in \(d/\epsilon\) on a constructed experiment.

related_work:
Zhao et al. are the closest general-function reverse-KL comparator, not a tabular-only result. In their offline i.i.d. model the reference policy equals the behavior policy and the reward class \(\mathcal G\) is general and realizable. Their Theorem 2.10 gives, for sufficiently small \(\epsilon\), the high-probability sample-complexity upper bound \(\widetilde O\!\left(\eta D_{\pi^\star}^2\epsilon^{-1}\log N_{\mathcal G}(\epsilon)\right)\). For a linear class \(\mathcal G_\Theta=\{\phi^\top\vartheta:\vartheta\in\Theta\}\), their pointwise coefficient is
\[
D_{\mathcal G}^2((x,a);\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})=\sup_{\delta\in\Theta-\Theta}\frac{\{\phi(x,a)^\top\delta\}^2}{\delta^\top\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}\delta}.
\]
Only when \(\Theta-\Theta\) contains a nonzero multiple of every needed direction does this equal \(\phi(x,a)^\top\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1}\phi(x,a)\). Under that directional-richness condition, \(D_{\pi^\star}^2=\operatorname{tr}(M)\), where \(M=\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1/2}\Lambda_P^\star\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1/2}\), and therefore \(D_P\le D_{\pi^\star}^2\le dD_P\). The bounded prediction polytope alone does not imply directional richness; without it, only \(D_{\mathcal G}^2((x,a);\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})\le\phi(x,a)^\top\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-1}\phi(x,a)\) is automatic, not the trace identity or the lower comparison with \(D_P\). Thus the spectral factor can be up to \(d\) smaller than the trace factor in the directionally rich specialization, but the present bounded shared-linear, all-temperature, expected-minimax exact-shell theorem does not wholesale dominate Zhao et al.'s general-function, sufficiently-small-accuracy, high-probability result. Their Theorem 2.11 is existential over a density-ratio upper bound \(C^\star\), not a lower bound on an exact \((C_P,D_P)\) shell. Ji et al. provide the complementary matched tabular multi-armed-bandit frontier.

Li--Ma--Srebro study unregularized offline linear contextual bandits with fixed logged covariates and a known test distribution. Their \(\ell_p\)-confidence-set rules maximize a pessimistic unregularized value over deterministic policies; for PUNC, Theorem 1 controls \(V(\pi^\star)-V(\widehat\pi)\) at an \(n^{-1/2}\) rate through the whitened first-moment quantity \(\|\Sigma_{\mathcal D}^{-1/2}\mathbb E_\rho\phi(s,\pi^\star(s))\|_1\). The learner here instead selects a confidence-set member minimizing a worst empirical Gibbs-weighted squared radius and deploys its stochastic Gibbs policy; its loss is reverse-KL-regularized welfare, and its coverage quantity \(D_P\) is the largest generalized eigenvalue of target and logging feature second moments. Li--Ma--Srebro therefore supply the linear-pessimism precedent but do not imply the bound \(\widetilde O(\min\{\eta dD/n,\sqrt{dD/n}\})\) or its all-temperature sample-complexity inversion.

Nguyen-Tang--Arora characterize broad unregularized offline contextual-bandit classes using policy-transfer coefficients and pseudo-dimension: Theorem 4.1 gives an information-theoretic class lower bound and Theorem 5.1 analyzes the OfDM-Hedge actor--critic learner. Their Example 3.3 already demonstrates that zero policy suboptimality can coexist with a vacuous concentrability coefficient. Accordingly, the present note does not claim novelty for the general observation that coarse coverage can overstate difficulty. Its narrower theorem fixes the reverse-KL Gibbs objective and exact \((C_P,D_P)\) equalities, gives a finite fixed-design shell-feasibility certificate, and constructs two public experiments with the same \((d,C,D,\eta)\) but different minimax frontiers; those conclusions do not follow from the policy-transfer theorems.

Chen et al.'s Theorem 1 develops an interactive Fano framework that recovers classical Fano, Le Cam, and Assouad arguments, while their Theorems 10 and 15 characterize interactive model classes through fractional covering and DEC quantities. The paired sign-cube argument used here belongs to that information-theoretic lineage, but the present data are passive i.i.d. observations and Chen et al. do not establish exact reverse-KL-shell feasibility or same-index public-experiment nonuniqueness. Vannella et al.'s passive contextual-linear BPI Theorem 2 gives a fixed-confidence PAC-learnability condition and an instance-dependent information lower bound determined by the logged feature span and design matrix. That result concerns identifying an approximately optimal unregularized deterministic policy with confidence \(1-\delta\), rather than expected reverse-KL-regularized regret, exact \((C,D)\) shells, or a zero-risk-versus-local-\(d/\epsilon\) minimax comparison.

The primary-source basis for these comparisons is: \href{https://arxiv.org/html/2502.06051v3}{Zhao et al., Section 2.1, Definitions 2.4--2.5, Remark 2.6, Assumptions 2.7--2.8, Theorems 2.10--2.11, and Appendix B}, \href{https://papers.nips.cc/paper\_files/paper/2022/file/8443219a991f068c34d9491ad68ffa94-Paper-Conference.pdf}{Li--Ma--Srebro, Problem Setup and Theorem 1}, \href{https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10572972}{Nguyen-Tang--Arora, Sections 3--5}, \href{https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper\_files/paper/2024/file/8a23a95e26d016711c0d70f79ade3c95-Paper-Conference.pdf}{Chen et al., Theorems 1, 10, and 15}, and \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.02169}{Vannella et al.}.
interpretation: Feature coverage \(D\) is sufficient for the universal clean reverse-KL upper bound, so additional pointwise coverage \(C\) is statistically irrelevant for that achievability guarantee. Prior work already shows more generally that coverage summaries can overstate or incompletely describe offline difficulty. The specific conclusion here is that even the simultaneous exact indices \((d,C,D,\eta)\) fail to determine the fixed-public-experiment reverse-KL frontier: two experiments at those indices can have sample complexity one and a diverging pointwise local \(d/\epsilon\) lower rate. Reference support in the displayed learner class is solely a finite-objective representation: under extended reverse KL, every off-support output at a positive-mass context has infinite regret, and public measurable support repair proves equality with the full-simplex minimax problem.
technical_internal_limitation: The stabilized learner is explicit and measurable but is an idealized global-optimization procedure; computational efficiency is not established. The informative lower constant is allowed to depend on \((C,D,\eta)\), so the construction proves neither uniform lower dependence on \(D\) or \(\eta\) nor a quadratic \(dD/\epsilon^2\) branch. For every specified finite experiment, the quadratic normalization tends to zero as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\). The reference-supported decision representation is not an additional statistical limitation: it has exactly the same minimax value as the full-simplex extended-reverse-KL formulation.
honest_scope: The universal mathematical result is the all-temperature feature-coverage upper bound over every nonempty fixed-design exact reverse-KL shell. Relative to Zhao et al., the lawful sharpening is only the bounded shared-linear spectral specialization: under directional richness, \(D_P\) is the largest eigenvalue while Zhao et al.'s single-policy quantity is the trace, but the bounded prediction polytope alone does not guarantee that identity, and the present theorem does not dominate their general-function, sufficiently-small-accuracy, high-probability result. Relative to Li--Ma--Srebro, the novelty claim concerns reverse-KL Gibbs welfare and second-moment spectral coverage, not the origin of offline linear pessimism. The fixed-design theorem specializes, rather than supersedes, the broader coverage-insufficiency and information-complexity perspectives of Nguyen-Tang--Arora, Chen et al., and Vannella et al. Lower matching remains limited to a pointwise local \(\Omega_{C,D,\eta}(d/\epsilon)\) result on one informative experiment, while another experiment at the same indices has zero minimax risk; there is no uniform \(D\)- or \(\eta\)-dependent converse and no persistent quadratic lower branch. Finally, the stabilizing learner is defined by exact measurable global optimization over compact prediction polytopes; no finite-precision algorithm or approximation-regret theorem is supplied. Throughout, the standard extended reverse-KL convention governs the full policy simplex. Restricting the written minimax infimum and diagnostic criterion to reference-supported policies only selects the finite-objective representation; the measurable public repair shows that this convention changes neither the minimax value nor any headline rate.
